newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: ESB sets out new strategy to face competition.
newsitem.headline: ESB sets out new strategy to face competition.

text.p: Ireland's Electricity Supply Board outlined a new business strategy aimed at ensuring the company's competitiveness when the Irish electricity market is opened to international competition for the first time.

"Despite facing competition for the first time in its history, the company's objective is to achieve profitable growth by defending its position in the Irish market against competitors and securing new market opportunities at home and abroad," the ESB said in a statement on Wednesday.
The ESB has set itself an initial target of achieving a 12 percent return on capital employed.
This target will be reviewed by the board every two years.

The ESB said it would continue to seek competitiveness in its core activties and remained determined to achieve, within three years, manpower and other cost savings which would result in a reduction in the numbers employed by 2,000 and annual net cost savings of 58 million punts.
It said it aimed to build a sound relationship with the new independent regulator.
The Irish government announced last year that it would allow competition in the construction, ownership and operation of power generation plants.
The ESB will continue to own and operate the high voltage national grid and the medium and low voltage distribution network.
But its monopoloy on the retail supply of electricity will be ended from January 1, 1998, for customers with peak demand of one megawatt or more.
An independent regulatory authority will also be established to issue licences and ensure fair and open competition.
